attribution.title: Marble Skill Taxonomy (v1)
attribution.standards: Curriculum standards referenced by the taxonomy have their own upstream licences (see PROVENANCE.md in that repository).
attribution.note: This is a starting point, not a diagnosis. Ages are approximate and the taxonomy is not written for learners with additional needs. Treat prerequisite links as a starting point and use professional judgement.

subject: Mathematics

topics.ds: Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10 using objects or drawings
e: Solve 'There are 6 apples, 2 are eaten, how many left?' using counters
Solve 'add to' and 'take from' result-unknown problems
Solve 'put together/take apart' problems with total unknown
topics.p: If you say 'There are 7 birds on a fence and 3 fly away — how many are left?', can {{name}} work it out using their fingers, counters, or a quick drawing?

topics.n: Addition as combining or putting together two
topics.ds: Understand addition as combining or putting together two groups to find the total
e: Model 'putting together' with physical objects and say the total
Act out an 'add to' situation (e.g. 3 children arrive, then 2 more join)
Explain that addition means finding how many altogether
topics.p: If {{name}} has 4 toy cars and a friend brings 3 more, do they understand that adding means combining both groups — and can they tell you there are now 7 cars altogether?

topics.ds: Find the number that makes 10 when added to a given number from 1 to 9 (number bonds to 10)
e: Given 7, respond '3' to make 10
Use a ten-frame to find the complement to 10
Record pairs that make 10 as equations (e.g. 6 + 4 = 10)
topics.p: If {{name}} has 6 strawberries and needs 10 for a recipe, can they quickly tell you they need 4 more — without counting all the way up from 1?

topics.ds: Decompose numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way (part-part-whole)
e: Use objects or drawings to find all pairs that make a given number
Record decompositions as equations
topics.p: If {{name}} has 8 grapes, can they split them into two groups in different ways — like 3 and 5, or 4 and 4 — and explain that both groups together still make 8?

topics.ds: Represent addition and subtraction using objects, drawings, and mental images
e: Use cubes or counters to show 3 + 2
Draw a picture to represent a subtraction situation
Use fingers to model an addition problem
topics.p: If {{name}} has 3 apples and you give them 2 more, can they show you how many there are altogether — using their fingers, some small objects, or a drawing?

topics.n: Subtraction as taking away or separating
topics.ds: Understand subtraction as taking away or separating from a group to find how many remain
e: Model 'taking away' with physical objects and say how many remain
Act out a 'take from' situation (e.g. 5 biscuits, eat 2, how many left?)
Explain that subtraction means finding how many are left
topics.p: If {{name}} has 9 biscuits and eats 3, do they understand that subtracting means taking some away — and can they tell you 6 biscuits are left?

topics.ds: Add and subtract one-digit and two-digit numbers to 20, including zero
e: Calculate 14 + 5 = 19
Calculate 17 – 3 = 14
Add or subtract 0 and explain the result stays the same
topics.p: Can {{name}} work out sums like '14 + 5' or '18 − 6' in their head or on paper, and do they know that adding or taking away zero leaves the number unchanged?

topics.ds: Solve one-step word problems involving addition and subtraction to 20, including missing-number problems
e: Solve 'I have 12 sweets and eat 4, how many left?'
Solve missing number: 7 = [ ] – 9
Solve problems using concrete objects and pictorial representations
topics.p: If you say 'I had some sweets, ate 5, and now have 9 left — how many did I start with?', can {{name}} figure out the missing number?

topics.ds: Fluently add and subtract within 5
e: Answer 2 + 3 quickly without counting on fingers
Answer 5 – 2 from recall or with minimal counting
Complete a set of within-5 addition/subtraction facts accurately and quickly
topics.p: Can {{name}} give you the answer to sums like '2 + 3' or '5 − 2' straight away, without needing to count on their fingers every time?

topics.ds: Recall number bonds (addition and related subtraction facts) within 20
e: Quickly recall that 8 + 5 = 13
Given 13 – 5, respond 8 using knowledge of related addition fact
Know all pairs of single-digit numbers that sum to numbers up to 20
topics.p: Can {{name}} quickly recall facts like '8 + 7 = 15' and immediately know that '15 − 7 = 8' — without having to work out the subtraction from scratch?

topics.ds: Represent practical addition, subtraction and quantity situations within 10 with virtual materials (on-screen counters and ten frames) as well as physical counters, using counting or subitising to find the result
e: Show '4 frogs on a log, 3 more jump on' by dragging counters onto an on-screen ten frame and say there are 7
Show '9 balloons, 2 pop' by removing counters in a counting app and say how many are left
Model the same story with real counters and with on-screen counters and explain that both show the same total
topics.p: If {{name}} plays a counting app where they drag frogs onto a log, can they show '4 frogs, then 3 more jump on' on screen and tell you there are 7 — and do the same with real buttons?

topics.ds: Read, write, and interpret the symbols +, −, and = in number sentences
e: Read 3 + 2 = 5 aloud as 'three plus two equals five'
Write a number sentence to match a concrete addition situation
Interpret the = sign as 'is the same as' rather than just 'the answer is'
topics.p: If you write '4 + 3 = 7' on paper, can {{name}} tell you what the plus sign, minus sign, and equals sign each mean?

topics.ds: Partition one-digit numbers and add and subtract within 20 using virtual materials (on-screen ten frames, counters and number lines) as well as physical materials, applying part-part-whole knowledge to 10 and make-ten strategies
e: Partition 8 on an on-screen ten frame as 5 and 3 and then as 6 and 2, writing a number sentence for each
Solve 8 + 5 on a virtual double ten frame by moving 2 counters to fill the first frame and adding the remaining 3
Solve 15 - 7 by removing counters on an on-screen twenty frame, then check it with real counters
topics.p: If {{name}} uses a maths app with ten frames, can they work out 8 + 5 by filling up the first ten frame — and check it with real counters?

topics.ds: Add and subtract a two-digit number and tens mentally and using concrete/pictorial representations
e: Calculate 45 + 30 = 75 mentally
Calculate 82 − 40 = 42 mentally
Explain that only the tens digit changes when adding/subtracting tens
topics.p: Can {{name}} quickly work out '54 + 30' or '78 − 20' in their head — knowing that only the tens digit changes?

topics.ds: Add three one-digit numbers using strategies including looking for pairs that make 10
e: Calculate 5 + 7 + 3 by first adding 7 + 3 = 10, then 5 + 10 = 15
Add any three single-digit numbers correctly
Identify useful pairs within three addends to make the calculation easier
topics.p: If {{name}} needs to add 4 + 6 + 8, can they spot that 4 and 6 make 10 first, then add 8 to get 18 — rather than just adding in order from left to right?

topics.ds: Add and subtract two two-digit numbers using concrete objects, pictorial representations, and mental methods
e: Calculate 34 + 27 using base-ten blocks or column addition
Calculate 63 − 28 using a number line or partitioning
Explain a strategy for adding or subtracting two two-digit numbers
topics.p: Can {{name}} add or subtract two two-digit numbers — like '43 + 28' — using counters, a drawing, or working it out in their head?

topics.ds: Add within 100 using strategies based on place value, including adding a two-digit and one-digit number, and a two-digit and a multiple of 10
e: Calculate 46 + 7 using place value (46 + 4 + 3 = 53)
Calculate 38 + 40 = 78 using tens understanding
Relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning
topics.p: Can {{name}} work out sums like '47 + 8' or '35 + 50' by thinking about the tens and ones separately rather than counting up one at a time?

topics.ds: Use counting on and counting back as strategies for addition and subtraction
e: Add 8 + 3 by starting at 8 and counting on 3 (9, 10, 11)
Subtract 12 − 3 by counting back 3 from 12 (11, 10, 9)
Explain that counting on is a way to add
topics.p: If {{name}} needs to work out '8 + 5', can they start from 8 and count up five more — rather than starting from 1 every time?

topics.ds: Add and subtract within 20 using strategies such as making ten, decomposing a number leading to ten, and using known facts
e: Solve 8 + 6 using making ten: 8 + 2 + 4 = 14
Solve 13 − 4 by decomposing: 13 − 3 − 1 = 9
Use a known fact (8 + 4 = 12) to derive 12 − 8 = 4
topics.p: If {{name}} needs to work out '8 + 6', can they split the 6 into 2 + 4, use the 2 to fill up to 10, then add the remaining 4 to get 14?

topics.ds: Understand and apply the commutative property of addition: addends can be added in any order
e: Explain that 3 + 8 gives the same answer as 8 + 3
Use commutativity to choose the larger number to count on from
Demonstrate that subtraction is not commutative (5 − 3 ≠ 3 − 5)
topics.p: Does {{name}} know that 6 + 4 gives the same answer as 4 + 6, so they can always choose whichever order makes the adding easier?

topics.n: Finding a missing number in addition
topics.ds: Understand subtraction as finding an unknown addend (e.g. 10 − 8 = ? is the same as 8 + ? = 10)
e: Solve 10 − 8 by thinking 'what do I add to 8 to make 10?'
Explain that subtraction can be thought of as a missing-addend problem
Use known addition facts to solve related subtraction problems
topics.p: Can {{name}} see that '10 − 8 = ?' is the same as asking 'what do I add to 8 to reach 10?' — so they can use their adding knowledge to help with subtraction?

topics.ds: Fluently add and subtract within 10
e: Answer any addition fact within 10 quickly from memory
Answer any subtraction fact within 10 quickly from memory
Complete a timed set of within-10 facts with high accuracy
topics.p: Can {{name}} answer sums like '7 + 3' or '9 − 4' almost instantly — without stopping to count on their fingers?

topics.ds: Recall and use addition and subtraction facts to 20 fluently, and derive and use related facts up to 100
e: Rapidly recall 7 + 8 = 15 and 15 − 8 = 7
Use 6 + 4 = 10 to derive 60 + 40 = 100
Derive 35 + 5 = 40 from knowledge that 5 + 5 = 10
topics.p: Can {{name}} quickly recall facts like '9 + 7 = 16' and '16 − 7 = 9', and use those to help work out bigger sums like '90 + 70'?

topics.ds: Understand and apply the associative property of addition: when adding three numbers, any two can be added first
e: Solve 2 + 6 + 4 by first adding 6 + 4 = 10, then 2 + 10 = 12
Explain that grouping addends differently gives the same total
Choose which two numbers to add first to make the calculation easier
topics.p: If {{name}} needs to add 3 + 7 + 6, can they spot that adding 3 and 7 first (to make 10) is easier — rather than always working left to right?

topics.ds: Recognise and use the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction to check calculations and solve missing-number problems
e: Check 15 + 7 = 22 by calculating 22 − 7 = 15
Use the inverse to solve: □ + 9 = 14, so □ = 14 − 9 = 5
Explain that addition and subtraction 'undo' each other
topics.p: If {{name}} works out 13 + 5 = 18, can they immediately use that to say '18 − 5 = 13' — without having to work the subtraction out all over again?

topics.ds: Add and subtract a two-digit number and ones mentally and using concrete/pictorial representations
e: Calculate 36 + 7 = 43 using objects or mentally
Calculate 52 − 4 = 48 using a number line or mentally
Explain bridging through 10 when adding ones to a two-digit number
topics.p: Can {{name}} work out '36 + 7' or '42 − 5' in their head — keeping the tens in place and only adjusting the ones?

topics.n: Mental and written addition and subtraction
topics.ds: Solve addition and subtraction problems using mental and written methods, including problems involving numbers, quantities, and measures
e: Solve a two-step problem: 'I had 35p, spent 12p, then found 5p. How much now?'
Choose an appropriate method (mental or written) for a given problem
Solve problems involving measures, e.g. 'a ribbon is 45cm, I cut off 18cm'
topics.p: If {{name}} is given a problem involving lengths, weights, or prices, can they decide whether to add or subtract and carry out the calculation correctly?

topics.ds: Subtract multiples of 10 (10–90) from multiples of 10 using place value strategies
e: Calculate 70 − 30 = 40
Use base-ten blocks to show 80 − 50 = 30
Explain that subtracting tens is like subtracting the tens digits
topics.p: Can {{name}} quickly work out '80 − 50' or '70 − 40' in their head by thinking about how many tens are left?

topics.ds: Solve word problems that call for adding three whole numbers with a total of 20 or less, representing the problem with objects, a drawing or a three-part bar model and with an equation that uses a symbol for the unknown total (e.g. 4 + 7 + 6 = ☐); choose a convenient order or grouping to add (such as making 10 first) and give the answer in the context of the problem
e: Solve 'Sam has 4 red, 7 blue and 6 green pencils. How many pencils does he have?' with counters or a drawing, writing 4 + 7 + 6 = ☐ and answering 'Sam has 17 pencils'
Write the equation 3 + 9 + 7 = ☐ for a story about apples picked on three days, and add 3 + 7 first to make 10 (19 apples)
Draw a three-part bar model for a story about 5 cars, 8 bikes and 2 buses and explain how each part matches a number in the equation 5 + 8 + 2 = ☐
topics.p: If {{name}} picks 4 apples, then 7, then 6, could they show the problem with objects or a drawing, write it as 4 + 7 + 6 = ?, and work out how many apples they have altogether?

topics.ds: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers
e: Solve 8 + ? = 11 and write 3
Solve 5 = □ − 3 and write 8
Solve 6 + 6 = □ and write 12
topics.p: If {{name}} sees '? + 6 = 14' or '9 − ? = 4' written on paper, can they figure out what number goes in the gap?

topics.ds: Understand the meaning of the equal sign as 'is the same as' and determine if equations are true or false
e: Explain that 6 = 6 is true because both sides are the same
Determine that 4 + 1 = 5 + 2 is false
Understand that = does not mean 'the answer comes next' — it means balance
topics.p: Does {{name}} understand that '=' means 'the same as', so they can tell you whether '4 + 3 = 8 − 1' is true or false?

topics.ds: Add and subtract numbers with up to three digits using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction
e: Set out a columnar addition correctly with digits aligned by place value
Carry out columnar subtraction with exchange (borrowing) when needed
Check the answer using the inverse operation or estimation
topics.p: Can {{name}} set out a sum like '347 + 265' or '512 − 278' in columns and work through it step by step, carrying or borrowing where needed?

topics.ds: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations
e: Add three or four two-digit numbers by grouping tens and ones
Look for pairs that make multiples of 10 to simplify addition
Explain the strategy used to combine multiple addends
topics.p: Can {{name}} add up four two-digit numbers — like '14 + 23 + 32 + 19' — by grouping them cleverly, rather than just plodding through from left to right?

topics.ds: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations
e: Explain why adding tens and ones separately gives the correct total
Describe why a compensation strategy works (e.g. 'I added 1 too many, so I subtract 1')
Use place-value language to justify a written method step by step
topics.p: If {{name}} works out '67 + 24' by splitting it into '60 + 20' and '7 + 4', can they explain to you in words *why* that approach gives the right answer?

topics.ds: Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models, drawings, and strategies based on place value; understand composing and decomposing tens and hundreds
e: Add two three-digit numbers using base-ten blocks or drawings, composing a ten or hundred when necessary
Subtract three-digit numbers, decomposing a ten or hundred when necessary
Relate the concrete/drawn strategy to a written method and explain why it works
topics.p: Can {{name}} add or subtract numbers in the hundreds — like '347 + 256' — by thinking about hundreds, tens, and ones separately, or drawing a diagram to help?

topics.ds: Estimate the answer to a calculation and use inverse operations to check answers; apply to increasingly large numbers using rounding and inverse reasoning
e: Round numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 to estimate a sum or difference before calculating
Use addition to check a subtraction answer, or vice versa
Identify when a calculated answer is unreasonable based on the estimate
Round numbers to estimate a sum or difference before calculating
Use addition to check a subtraction answer and vice versa
Identify an unreasonable answer by comparing to the estimate
topics.p: Before {{name}} works out a calculation, can they make a sensible rough guess — and then check their answer using the opposite operation?

topics.ds: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction
e: Add two-digit numbers within 100 efficiently (e.g. 46 + 37 using place-value partitioning)
Subtract two-digit numbers within 100 fluently (e.g. 83 − 25)
Choose between strategies (decomposing, compensating, using known facts) based on the numbers involved
topics.p: Can {{name}} reliably add or subtract two-digit numbers like '68 + 27' or '91 − 45', choosing the best strategy for each problem?

topics.ds: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies; know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers
e: Answer any single-digit addition fact within 3 seconds
Recall subtraction facts within 20 from memory (e.g. 15 − 8 = 7)
Use known addition facts to derive related subtraction facts rapidly
topics.p: Can {{name}} instantly recall all the single-digit addition facts — like '7 + 8 = 15' — without needing to count or think for more than a second?

topics.ds: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and ones
e: Calculate 345 + 7 mentally
Calculate 462 − 5 mentally
Explain that only the ones digit changes (unless bridging through a ten)
topics.p: Can {{name}} work out '436 + 7' or '521 − 8' in their head — keeping the hundreds and tens unchanged while adjusting just the ones?

topics.ds: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and hundreds
e: Calculate 345 + 200 mentally
Calculate 762 − 400 mentally
Explain that only the hundreds digit changes
topics.p: Can {{name}} quickly work out '342 + 200' or '756 − 300' in their head — knowing that only the hundreds digit changes?

topics.ds: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and tens
e: Calculate 345 + 40 mentally
Calculate 462 − 30 mentally
Explain that only the tens digit changes (unless bridging through a hundred)
topics.p: Can {{name}} quickly work out '354 + 40' or '628 − 30' in their head — knowing that only the tens digit changes?

topics.ds: Solve addition and subtraction problems including missing-number problems, using number facts, place value, and more complex methods
e: Solve a missing-number problem such as 245 + ? = 380
Choose an appropriate method (mental, written, or combination) based on the numbers
Solve multi-step problems combining addition and subtraction of three-digit numbers
topics.p: Can {{name}} work out sums with a hidden number — like '? − 38 = 24' or '53 + ? = 91' — by thinking carefully about what the equation is asking?

topics.ds: Represent whole numbers as lengths on a number line and represent sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram
e: Place whole numbers on a number line with equally spaced points
Show an addition as a jump forward on the number line (e.g. 38 + 27 shown as jumps)
Show a subtraction as a jump backward on the number line
topics.p: Can {{name}} mark numbers on a number line and show what happens when they add or subtract — for example, jumping forward 35 places from 48?

topics.ds: Solve one- and two-step word problems within 100 using addition and subtraction, with unknowns in all positions
e: Solve a two-step word problem involving adding to and taking from
Represent a word problem with an equation using a symbol for the unknown
Solve comparison problems (how many more/fewer) within 100
topics.p: If a word problem says 'Sam had 78 stickers, gave some away, and now has 45 — how many did he give away?', can {{name}} work out which operation to use and find the answer?

topics.ds: Add and subtract numbers with up to four digits using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction
e: Set out and solve a columnar addition with up to four-digit numbers
Set out and solve a columnar subtraction with exchange across multiple columns
Check the answer using estimation or inverse operations
topics.p: Can {{name}} line up a sum like '3,842 + 1,765' or '4,301 − 2,658' in columns and work through it correctly — carrying and borrowing across multiple columns?

topics.ds: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction
e: Add two three-digit numbers fluently using an efficient method
Subtract three-digit numbers fluently, including with regrouping
Choose the most efficient strategy based on the numbers involved
topics.p: Can {{name}} add or subtract three-digit numbers like '672 − 348' reliably, choosing whichever method works best for them?

topics.ds: Solve addition and subtraction two-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why
e: Identify the two steps needed to solve a contextual problem
Choose between mental and written methods for each step based on the numbers
Explain why the chosen operations and methods are appropriate
topics.p: If {{name}} reads a word problem with two steps — like working out change from a shopping trip with two items — can they plan which calculations to do and in what order?

topics.ds: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations; represent problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity
e: Solve a two-step problem that combines addition/subtraction with multiplication/division
Write an equation using a letter for the unknown (e.g. 3 × n + 5 = 26)
Assess the reasonableness of the answer using estimation and mental computation
topics.p: Can {{name}} write an equation like 'n + 25 = 60' to represent a word problem, and then solve it to find what n equals?

topics.ds: Solve addition and subtraction multi-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why
e: A school collects 12,450 bottles in Week 1 and 8,372 in Week 2; their target is 25,000 — how many more do they need?
Choose between mental and written methods for each step and explain why
Solve a three-step problem involving addition and subtraction of five-digit numbers
topics.p: If {{name}} is given a multi-step problem — like planning a budget where money is added and spent in several steps — can they decide which operations to use at each stage and explain their thinking?

topics.ds: Use rounding to check answers to calculations and determine appropriate levels of accuracy in context
e: Check 47,832 + 23,156 ≈ 48,000 + 23,000 = 71,000 to verify the exact answer 70,988
Decide whether to round to the nearest 100 or 1,000 for a given estimation context
Identify that a calculated answer of 3,421 cannot be correct because the estimate gives approximately 50,000
topics.p: If {{name}} gets an answer of 4,213 for an addition, can they round the numbers to double-check — like '4,000 + 1,000 ≈ 5,000' — and spot if the answer seems way off?

topics.ds: Fluently add and subtract whole numbers with more than four digits using the standard columnar algorithm
e: Calculate 34,567 + 28,945 using columnar addition
Calculate 500,000 − 234,178 using columnar subtraction with multiple exchanges
Add three five-digit numbers in a single column layout
topics.p: Can {{name}} accurately add or subtract large numbers — like '23,846 + 14,579' — using the column method, carrying and borrowing correctly however many columns it takes?

topics.ds: Add and subtract numbers mentally with increasingly large numbers, using place-value knowledge and derived facts
e: Mentally calculate 45,000 + 8,000
Mentally subtract 3,200 from 10,000 by counting up
Use near-doubles: 2,500 + 2,600 = 5,100
topics.p: Can {{name}} work out something like '4,700 − 1,300' in their head using what they know about place value — without needing to write it all out?

topics.ds: Solve addition and subtraction multi-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why, with numbers up to 10,000,000 and decimals
e: Solve a two-step word problem involving addition and subtraction of numbers beyond 1,000,000
Choose between mental, written, and calculator methods for a multi-step problem and justify the choice
Interpret a real-life context to identify which addition/subtraction operations are needed across multiple steps
topics.p: If {{name}} is given a complicated word problem involving large numbers or decimals — like calculating the total cost of several items — can they plan and carry out all the steps correctly?

topics.ds: Add and subtract decimals to hundredths using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate strategies to written methods and explain reasoning
e: Correctly compute 3.45 + 2.78 and explain regrouping across decimal places
Use a number line or base-ten blocks to model 5.03 − 2.67
Explain why the standard algorithm works for decimal addition by connecting to place-value understanding
topics.p: Can {{name}} add or subtract decimal amounts like '4.73 + 2.68' or '10.00 − 3.47', lining up the decimal points and working through the columns correctly?

topics.ds: Understand positive and negative numbers as describing quantities with opposite directions or values; use them in context such as temperature, floors in a building, and bank balances
e: Represent positive and negative numbers on a number line and explain what zero means in context
Add a positive or negative number to any integer using number line reasoning
Subtract a positive or negative number from any integer, understanding that subtracting a negative is equivalent to adding
topics.p: If {{name}} sees temperatures like −3°C and +5°C on a weather forecast, can they figure out how much warmer one day is than the other — even when the answer crosses zero?

topics.ds: Identify and describe the repeating unit (core) of a repeating pattern made with numbers, symbols, shapes or objects, and use it to continue, create and compare patterns
e: Circle the part that repeats in red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue and describe it as an ABB pattern
Build a new pattern with the unit 1, 2, 2, 3 and repeat it three times
Say whether clap, stamp, stamp, clap, stamp, stamp and circle, square, square have the same repeating unit
topics.p: If {{name}} sees beads threaded red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, can they point out the part that keeps repeating and use it to make their own pattern?

topics.ds: Recognise, describe and create additive patterns that increase or decrease by a constant amount using numbers, shapes and objects, state the rule, and find missing elements
e: Describe 5, 8, 11, 14 as 'start at 5 and add 3 each time'
Find the missing numbers in 40, 35, __, 25, __, 15
Build a tower pattern that grows by 2 blocks each step and predict the 6th tower
topics.p: If {{name}} sees the house numbers 5, 8, 11, 14 along a street, can they say the numbers go up by 3 each time and work out what comes next?

topics.ds: Follow and create algorithms (flowcharts or written step lists) with a sequence of steps, decisions using comparisons (e.g. 'Is the number greater than 20?', 'Is it even?') and repetition until a stop condition, to investigate numbers and describe the patterns that emerge
e: Follow a flowchart: start at 7; if the number is even halve it, otherwise add 1; repeat until you reach 1, and record each number
Describe what a flowchart with the decision 'Is the number greater than 50?' does to the numbers 34, 51 and 80
Write a step-by-step algorithm with one decision that sorts a list of numbers into 'less than 10' and '10 or more'
topics.p: If {{name}} is given a set of instructions like 'if the number is even, halve it; if it's odd, add 1; keep going until you reach 1', can they follow it step by step and notice any pattern?

topics.ds: Follow and create algorithms with steps and decisions that use addition or multiplication to generate sets of numbers (e.g. repeated doubling or adding a constant until a limit), and identify and describe the patterns produced
e: Follow 'start at 3, double the number, stop when it is greater than 100' and list the numbers made
Create an algorithm that adds 7 repeatedly from 0 and stops before 80, then describe the pattern in the ones digits
Explain why an algorithm that multiplies by 5 always produces numbers ending in 0 or 5
topics.p: If {{name}} follows the rule 'start at 3 and keep doubling until you go past 100', can they list the numbers and spot a pattern in them?

topics.ds: Design and use algorithms with a sequence of steps, decisions with several alternatives (if / else-if / else) and repetition that apply rules to generate sets of numbers, implementing them in a flowchart, spreadsheet or visual program, and explain the patterns produced
e: Design a flowchart that classifies each number from 1 to 30 as 'multiple of 3', 'multiple of 5', 'both' or 'neither' and repeats for every number
Implement 'start at 1; repeat 10 times: multiply by 2 and add 1' in a spreadsheet or block program and list the numbers made
Explain why every number generated by the 'multiply by 2 and add 1' algorithm is odd
topics.p: Could {{name}} design a set of instructions — like a flowchart or a simple spreadsheet — that sorts every number from 1 to 30 into groups such as 'multiple of 3', 'multiple of 5' or 'both', and explain the pattern?

topics.ds: Find pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns (e.g. find pairs (a, b) where a + b = 10 or 2a + b = 15)
e: List all whole-number pairs (a, b) where a + b = 12 with a, b > 0
Find three pairs that satisfy 2x + y = 20
Explain systematically how to generate all integer solutions to a two-variable equation within a given range
topics.p: Can {{name}} find different pairs of numbers that both satisfy a rule — for example, all the pairs of whole numbers that add up to 10?

topics.ds: Generate and describe linear number sequences, including those with negative and decimal steps; identify the term-to-term rule
e: Continue the sequence 2.5, 4.0, 5.5, ... and state the rule as 'add 1.5'
Generate terms of a sequence that crosses zero (e.g. 3, 1, −1, −3, ...)
Describe the term-to-term rule for a given linear sequence and predict the 10th term
topics.p: If {{name}} sees a number sequence like 3, 7, 11, 15… can they describe the rule, continue it, and predict what the 10th number will be?

topics.ds: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules; identify relationships between corresponding terms; form ordered pairs and graph them on a coordinate plane
e: Generate sequences starting at 0 with rules 'add 3' and 'add 6'; observe terms in one are twice the other
Form ordered pairs from corresponding terms and plot them on a coordinate grid
Explain informally why the relationship between the two sequences holds
topics.p: Can {{name}} follow two number patterns at once — for example, "add 2" and "add 4" — pair up the matching terms, and plot those pairs as points on a graph?

topics.ds: Enumerate possibilities of combinations of two variables systematically (e.g. all ways to choose from a set of options)
e: List all possible meal combinations from 3 starters and 4 mains
Organise combinations into a systematic table to ensure none are missed
Explain why the total number of combinations equals the product of the options in each category
topics.p: If {{name}} can choose any combination of 3 T-shirt colours and 2 trouser colours, can they list every possible outfit without missing any or repeating?

topics.ds: Use simple formulae expressed in words or symbols to calculate values (e.g. perimeter = 2 × (length + width))
e: Substitute values into P = 2(l + w) to find the perimeter of a rectangle
Use the formula for area of a triangle (A = 1/2 × b × h) given base and height values
Interpret a formula expressed in words and use it to compute an output
topics.p: If {{name}} is told that the perimeter of a rectangle uses the formula perimeter = 2 × (length + width), can they plug in the measurements and work out the answer?

topics.ds: Express missing number problems algebraically using letters for unknowns; translate word problems into equations
e: Write 'I think of a number, double it, and add 5 to get 17' as 2n + 5 = 17
Solve a one-step equation such as 3x = 24 and explain the reasoning
Express a word problem as an algebraic equation and find the unknown value
topics.p: If {{name}} reads "I think of a number, double it, and add 5 to get 17," can they write that as an equation using a letter for the unknown and solve it?

topics.ds: Use and interpret algebraic notation including: ab for a × b, 3y for y + y + y, a² for a × a, a/b for a ÷ b, coefficients as fractions, and brackets for grouping; read and write algebraic expressions fluently
e: Read and interpret expressions using standard algebraic conventions for multiplication, division, and powers
Write algebraic expressions from word descriptions using correct notation
Understand that juxtaposition means multiplication and that a/b means a divided by b
topics.p: When {{name}} sees something written as "3y" or "a²" in a maths problem, do they know what those shorthand notations mean and can they work with them?

topics.ds: Model situations or procedures by translating them into algebraic expressions or formulae and by using graphs; move between word problems, algebraic representations, tables, and graphical representations
e: Translate a word problem or real-world situation into an algebraic expression or formula
Construct a table of values from an algebraic rule
Plot the corresponding graph and interpret it in the context of the problem
topics.p: Can {{name}} take a real-world situation — like a taxi that charges £2 plus £1.50 per mile — and write an algebraic formula for the total cost, then sketch what the graph looks like?

topics.ds: Simplify algebraic expressions by collecting like terms — combine terms with the same variable and power (e.g., 3a + 2b + 5a = 8a + 2b) while maintaining equivalence
e: Identify like terms in an algebraic expression
Combine like terms involving positive and negative coefficients
Simplify expressions involving multiple variables and constant terms
topics.p: If {{name}} sees an expression like "5a + 3b + 2a," can they simplify it by collecting the like terms to get "7a + 3b"?

topics.ds: Plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants of the Cartesian plane, using positive and negative x- and y-values to describe positions precisely
e: Plot points with negative coordinates accurately in all four quadrants
Identify the quadrant a point belongs to from its coordinate signs
Read coordinates from a graph including fractional and negative values
topics.p: Can {{name}} plot a point like (−3, 4) correctly on a coordinate grid and read the coordinates of points in all four quadrants, including negative numbers?

topics.ds: Expand (multiply out) a single term over a bracket using the distributive property, e.g., 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15; expand expressions involving negative multipliers
e: Multiply a single positive term over a bracket to expand the expression
Multiply a negative term over a bracket, correctly handling signs
Combine expanding brackets with collecting like terms to simplify fully
topics.p: Can {{name}} expand a bracket like 3(2x + 5) by multiplying everything inside, to get 6x + 15?

topics.ds: Understand and use the concepts and vocabulary of expressions, equations, inequalities, terms, and factors; distinguish between an expression (no equals sign), an equation (equals sign), and an inequality (inequality sign)
e: Define and distinguish between expression, equation, and inequality
Identify terms, coefficients, and factors in algebraic expressions
Use the vocabulary of algebra precisely in mathematical discussions
topics.p: Can {{name}} explain the difference between an expression like "3x + 2," an equation like "3x + 2 = 11," and an inequality like "3x + 2 > 11"?

topics.ds: Generate terms of a sequence from a term-to-term rule (e.g., 'add 3 each time') or a position-to-term rule (e.g., '2n + 1'), and identify whether a sequence is arithmetic, geometric, or neither
e: Continue a sequence given a term-to-term rule involving addition, subtraction, or multiplication
Generate the first five terms from a position-to-term formula such as 3n − 2
Classify sequences as arithmetic (constant difference), geometric (constant ratio), or other
topics.p: Can {{name}} work out the next few terms of a sequence like 5, 8, 11, 14… and explain whether the rule is "add a fixed number each time" or something else?

topics.ds: Understand inequalities as statements comparing expressions, represent solutions on a number line, and solve simple linear inequalities using the same inverse-operation methods as equations
e: Write an inequality from a worded constraint (e.g., 'must be at least 12' → x ≥ 12)
Represent the solution set of an inequality on a number line with open or closed circles
Solve a one-step or two-step inequality such as 3x + 1 < 10
topics.p: Can {{name}} solve an inequality like 2x + 1 < 9, show the answer on a number line, and explain what all the solutions have in common?

topics.ds: Use algebraic methods to solve linear equations in one variable, including equations that require rearrangement, expanding brackets, and collecting terms on both sides; solve equations with rational number coefficients
e: Solve one-step and two-step linear equations in one variable
Solve equations requiring expansion of brackets and collection of like terms
Solve equations with the unknown on both sides and with fractional or negative coefficients
topics.p: If {{name}} is given an equation like 3x + 7 = 22, can they work through the steps to find the value of x?

topics.ds: Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions including scientific formulae; evaluate expressions by replacing variables with given values and computing the result using correct order of operations
e: Substitute positive and negative values into algebraic expressions and evaluate
Substitute values into formulae involving multiple operations and powers
Use correct order of operations when evaluating expressions after substitution
topics.p: If a formula says that the area of a triangle is ½ × base × height, can {{name}} substitute in the measurements and calculate the answer correctly?

topics.ds: Factorise algebraic expressions by taking out common factors — identify the highest common factor of all terms and write the expression as a product, e.g., 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)
e: Identify the highest common factor of all terms in an expression
Write the factorised form as a product of the HCF and a bracket
Check factorisation by expanding the brackets back out
topics.p: Can {{name}} look at an expression like "6x + 9" and rewrite it with the common factor taken out — as "3(2x + 3)"?

topics.ds: Recognise that a linear function produces a straight-line graph, understand the relationship between an equation of the form y = mx + c and its graphical representation, and interpret gradient and y-intercept in context
e: Explain that changing m in y = mx + c alters the steepness and direction of the line
Identify the y-intercept of a line from its equation and from its graph
Determine whether a given equation will produce a straight line or a curve
topics.p: If {{name}} sees the equation y = 2x + 3, can they explain what the graph will look like — including how steep it is and where it crosses the y-axis?

topics.ds: Find the nth-term expression for an arithmetic sequence by identifying the common difference and the zero-term, and use it to determine any term in the sequence or test whether a given number belongs to the sequence
e: Derive the nth-term rule for an arithmetic sequence such as 3, 7, 11, 15, … as 4n − 1
Use an nth-term formula to find the 50th or 100th term without listing all preceding terms
Determine whether a given number (e.g., 99) is a term in a specified arithmetic sequence
topics.p: If {{name}} is given the sequence 4, 7, 10, 13…, can they find a formula for the nth term — and use it to check whether, say, 100 is in the sequence?

topics.ds: Plot linear graphs by generating a table of values, reduce a two-variable linear equation to the form y = mx + c, and calculate gradients from two points on a line
e: Generate a table of (x, y) values for a linear equation and plot the points accurately
Rearrange an equation such as 2x + 3y = 12 into the form y = mx + c
Calculate the gradient between two coordinate points using rise over run
topics.p: Can {{name}} draw the graph of a straight line by making a table of values and plotting the points — and work out the gradient from two points on the line?

topics.ds: Understand and use standard mathematical formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject, performing inverse operations to isolate a different variable
e: Identify the subject of a given formula
Use inverse operations to rearrange a formula to make a different variable the subject
Rearrange formulae involving multiple steps including fractions and powers
topics.p: If a formula gives speed as distance ÷ time, can {{name}} rearrange it to find distance or time when they're the unknowns instead?

topics.ds: Use graphs of linear and quadratic functions to estimate output values for given inputs, find approximate solutions to equations, and interpret graphical information in real-world contexts
e: Read off an approximate y-value for a given x from a plotted curve
Find approximate solutions to an equation by identifying where a graph crosses the x-axis or another line
Interpret a real-world graph (e.g., distance–time) to answer contextual questions
topics.p: Can {{name}} use a graph — whether a straight line or a curve — to read off an answer to an equation approximately, rather than solving it algebraically?

topics.ds: Expand products of two or more binomials, e.g., (x + 3)(x - 2) = x² + x - 6, using the grid method or FOIL; simplify the result by collecting like terms
e: Expand the product of two binomials using a systematic method (grid or FOIL)
Collect like terms after expansion to simplify the result
Expand products involving negative terms correctly
topics.p: Can {{name}} multiply out two brackets like (x + 3)(x − 2) and collect the terms to get x² + x − 6?

topics.ds: Recognise that quadratic functions produce curved (parabolic) graphs, distinguish them from linear graphs, and use plotted quadratic graphs to estimate values and find approximate solutions
e: Explain why x² produces a U-shaped curve rather than a straight line
Plot a simple quadratic such as y = x² − 4 from a table of values
Read approximate solutions from a quadratic graph (e.g., where y = 0)
topics.p: Can {{name}} recognise that an equation like y = x² produces a curved graph rather than a straight line, and use a plotted curve to estimate values?

topics.ds: Understand that two linear equations can be solved simultaneously by finding the point where their graphs intersect, and interpret this graphically and algebraically as the pair of values satisfying both equations
e: Explain that the intersection of two lines represents values satisfying both equations
Find the approximate solution to a pair of simultaneous equations by reading a graph
Verify a proposed solution by substituting into both equations
topics.p: Can {{name}} explain that solving two equations simultaneously means finding the one pair of values that satisfies both at once — and show what that looks like on a graph?

topics.ds: Compare two groups of objects to determine which has more, fewer, or whether they are equal, using matching and counting strategies
e: Use one-to-one matching to compare two groups
State which group has more/fewer after counting both
Use the language 'equal to', 'more than', 'less than', 'fewer', 'most', 'least'
topics.p: If you put 6 raisins in one hand and 4 in the other and ask {{name}} which hand has more, can they work it out — either by counting or just by looking?

topics.ds: Cardinality principle: the last number said when counting a set tells how many objects are in the set, regardless of arrangement or order counted
e: After counting a set, answer 'how many?' with the last number stated
Understand that rearranging objects does not change the count
Understand that counting in a different order gives the same total
topics.p: If {{name}} counts out 7 toy cars and you ask "so how many cars are there?", do they say "7" straight away — or do they count them all again from the start?

topics.ds: Each successive counting number represents a quantity that is one larger than the previous number
e: Given a set of 5, know that adding one object makes 6
Explain that 8 is one more than 7
Given a number, identify one more and one less
topics.p: If {{name}} has 5 stickers and you give them one more, do they know immediately there are now 6 — without needing to count all of them again from one?

topics.ds: One-to-one correspondence when counting objects: each object is paired with exactly one number name
e: Point to or touch each object exactly once while saying number names
Do not skip objects or double-count when counting a set
Recognise an error when someone counts an object twice
topics.p: If {{name}} is counting a pile of grapes, do they touch or point to each one exactly once as they say each number — without skipping any or counting the same one twice?

topics.ds: Represent numbers using objects, pictorial representations, and the number line
e: Show a given number using counters, cubes, or fingers
Draw a pictorial representation of a quantity (e.g. tally marks, dots)
Locate a number on a number line
topics.p: If you ask {{name}} to show you what the number 5 looks like, can they do it in more than one way — such as drawing five dots, holding up five fingers, or pointing to 5 on a number line?

topics.ds: Count in multiples of 2, 5, and 10 (skip counting)
e: Count 2, 4, 6, 8 … up to at least 20
Count 5, 10, 15, 20 … up to at least 50
Count 10, 20, 30 … up to 100
topics.p: If {{name}} is counting socks being paired up, can they skip-count in twos — 2, 4, 6, 8 — all the way to 20? Can they also count up in fives when counting coins, or in tens on a number line?

topics.ds: Count a set of objects to answer 'how many?' for sets up to 20 (arranged in lines, arrays, circles, or scattered)
e: Accurately count up to 20 objects in a line
Count up to 10 scattered objects without losing track
Given a number 1–20, count out that many objects from a larger set
topics.p: If you spread out 15 buttons on the table in a random arrangement and ask {{name}} how many there are, can they count them all carefully and give you the right answer?

topics.ds: Rote count forwards and backwards from 0 to 100, beginning from 0, 1, or any given number, by ones
e: Recite the number sequence 1–100 without skipping or repeating
Count backward from 20 to 0
Count forward starting from a number other than 1 (e.g. 'start at 23')
topics.p: Can {{name}} count out loud all the way from 0 to 100 — and if you say "start from 47", can they carry on from there without going back to the beginning?

topics.ds: Use subitising to recognise and name the parts of a collection up to 10 and combine them — e.g. seeing 7 on a ten frame as 5 and 2, or a domino as 3 and 3 — connecting part-part-whole thinking to quick recognition
e: Look at a ten frame showing 7 and say 'five and two more makes seven' without counting every dot
Name the two parts on a domino showing 4 and 2 and say the total is 6
Show 8 as two groups (e.g. 4 and 4, or 5 and 3) and name the parts quickly
topics.p: If {{name}} looks at a domino with 4 dots on one side and 2 on the other, can they quickly say 'four and two make six' without counting every dot?

topics.ds: Recognise and name the number of objects in a collection of up to 5 instantly, without counting one by one (subitising), using dot patterns, dice faces, fingers and small groups of objects
e: Say how many dots are on a dice face showing 4 after a one-second glimpse, without counting
Show 3 fingers quickly without counting them up one at a time
Name the number in a flashed group of 2 or 5 counters arranged in different layouts
topics.p: When {{name}} rolls a dice in a board game, can they say how many dots there are straight away — without counting each dot?

topics.ds: Compare two written numerals between 1 and 10 to determine which is greater or less
e: Given two written numerals (e.g. 4 and 7), identify which is greater
Correctly use > and < or 'greater than' / 'less than' to compare single-digit numerals
topics.p: If you write "3" and "8" on two pieces of paper and ask {{name}} which number is bigger, can they get it right — and could they tell you why?

topics.ds: Quantify collections of up to 120 objects by partitioning them into equal groups (twos, fives or tens) and skip counting, explaining why grouping makes counting faster and more reliable
e: Count 85 pegs by sorting them into groups of ten and counting on 10, 20, ... 80, 85
Count 46 shoes by pairing them and skip counting by twos
Explain why counting 120 straws in bundles of ten is easier than counting one by one
topics.p: If {{name}} wants to know how many pasta shells are in a big jar, can they put them into groups of ten and count the groups to find the total?

topics.ds: Count forwards and backwards in steps of 3 from 0
e: Count 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 … up to at least 30
Count backwards in 3s from 30
Identify the next number in a sequence of multiples of 3
topics.p: Can {{name}} count in threes — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 — far enough to reach 30 without losing track or needing to start over?

topics.ds: Count forwards and backwards in tens from any number (not just multiples of 10)
e: Count 7, 17, 27, 37 … from a non-multiple starting point
Count backwards in tens from 83
Explain the pattern of adding/subtracting 10
topics.p: If {{name}} starts at 37 and you ask them to count up in tens, can they say 37, 47, 57, 67 — crossing over into the next hundred without getting stuck?

topics.ds: Count within 1000, including skip-counting by 5s, 10s, and 100s
e: Count forwards and backwards within 1000 from any starting number
Skip-count by 5s from any multiple of 5 to 1000
Skip-count by 100s from any number (e.g. 150, 250, 350 …)
topics.p: Can {{name}} count confidently up to 1000 — and if you ask them to count by hundreds from 200, or by tens from 650, can they do it without losing their place?

topics.ds: Count from 0 in multiples of 4, 8, 50, and 100
e: Recite the multiples of 4 from 0 to at least 48
Recite the multiples of 8 from 0 to at least 96
Count in steps of 50 and 100 from 0 to 1000
topics.p: Can {{name}} count in fours all the way to 48, count in eights, or count up in hundreds from any starting point — for example 350, 450, 550?

topics.ds: Count in multiples of 6, 7, 9, 25, and 1000
e: Recite the multiples of 6 from 0 to at least 72
Recite the multiples of 7 from 0 to at least 84
Count in steps of 25 from 0 to 1000 and in steps of 1000 up to 10,000
topics.p: Can {{name}} count in sevens — 7, 14, 21, 28 — or in nines, or in 25s when thinking about coins, or in 1000s when talking about distances like kilometres?

topics.ds: Interpret and construct simple pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams, and simple tables
e: Read a pictogram where each symbol represents one item
Construct a tally chart from collected data
Draw a block diagram to represent data from a survey
topics.p: Can {{name}} read a simple chart or pictogram — like one showing how many children chose each favourite fruit — and answer questions like "which was most popular"?

topics.ds: Classify objects into given categories, count the number in each category, and sort the categories by count
e: Sort a set of shapes by colour and count how many in each group
Sort objects by size (big/small) and state how many in each category
Identify which category has the most/fewest after sorting and counting
topics.p: Can {{name}} sort a pile of objects — like buttons, coins, or toy animals — into groups and count how many are in each group?

topics.ds: Use simple digital tools (graphing apps, tablet tally counters) to acquire and record categorical data from surveys, observations and simple experiments, display it as a list, table, picture or bar graph, and compare category frequencies
e: Enter class votes for favourite fruit into a graphing app to make a picture graph and say which fruit has the most and the fewest votes
Record a tally of birds seen using a tablet counting tool
Drop a paper cup 10 times, record whether it lands upright, upside down or on its side in a tablet tally app, and list the results in a table
topics.p: If {{name}} uses a tablet app at school to record a class vote, can they turn the results into a simple graph and say which choice was most popular?

topics.ds: Read, write, and use the vocabulary of data collection and display — data, tally, tally chart, frequency, frequency table, survey, pictogram, bar chart, axis/axes, scale, label, category, discrete data, continuous data, line graph, pie chart — and apply these terms when collecting, organising, and presenting data
e: Correctly label the axes of a bar chart including a title, axis labels, and scale
Distinguish between discrete data (counted) and continuous data (measured) with an example of each
Use 'tally', 'frequency', and 'pictogram' correctly when describing how to record and display data
topics.p: If {{name}} wanted to show you how many books different children in their class read last month, could they draw a bar chart, label the axes, and explain what each bar represents?

topics.ds: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories; solve put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph
e: Draw a picture graph with a symbol representing one unit for each data point
Draw a bar graph with labelled axes and a single-unit scale
Use a bar graph to answer comparison questions (e.g. 'How many more votes did cats get than dogs?')
topics.p: Can {{name}} draw a simple bar chart or picture graph to show information — like how many of each colour of sweet are in a bag — and answer questions from it?

topics.ds: Organise and represent data with up to three categories by counting objects in each category and sorting categories by quantity
e: Sort a set of objects into 2-3 given categories and count each group
Create a simple table or list showing category names and counts
Order categories from most to fewest or fewest to most
topics.p: Can {{name}} look at a collection of objects — like different coloured counters — sort them into up to three groups, count each group, and organise the results into a simple chart?

topics.ds: Interpret categorical data by asking and answering questions about totals, how many in each category, and how many more or less one category has than another
e: Answer 'how many?' for each category in a data set
Calculate the total number of data points across all categories
Compare two categories using 'how many more/fewer' language
topics.p: If {{name}} looks at a chart showing how many children chose each flavour of ice cream, can they answer questions like "how many chose chocolate?" and "how many more chose vanilla than strawberry?"

topics.ds: Compare different graphical representations of the same data (tally chart, picture graph, bar graph, list) and identify and describe the features each shows in response to questions
e: Show the same pet survey as a tally chart and as a picture graph and say what is the same in both
Explain which display makes it quicker to see the most popular pet
Answer the same question ('How many chose dogs?') from two different displays of the data
topics.p: If {{name}} sees a class pet survey shown as both a tally chart and a picture graph, can they explain what both show and which one makes the favourite easier to spot?

topics.ds: Interpret and present discrete and continuous data using appropriate graphical methods, including bar charts and time graphs
e: Read a time graph showing temperature changes over a day
Present data about plant growth over weeks as a time graph
Explain the difference between a bar chart (discrete) and a time graph (continuous)
topics.p: Can {{name}} choose the right type of chart for some data — for example, a bar chart for favourite colours or a line graph for temperature over a week — and draw it correctly?

topics.ds: Create and compare different representations of the same data set (table, scaled pictograph, bar graph), including with software, interpret the data in context, and choose the representation that best suits a purpose
e: Show the same sport survey as a table and as a bar graph made in software and describe what each makes easy to see
Choose a table to read an exact count and a bar graph to compare categories at a glance, explaining both choices
Interpret the bar graph by saying which sport is most popular and by how much
topics.p: If {{name}} has survey results, can they explain when a table is better (finding exact numbers) and when a bar graph is better (comparing at a glance)?

topics.ds: Acquire categorical and discrete numerical data to address a question of interest by observing, collecting or accessing a data set, and record it using appropriate methods including frequency tables and spreadsheets
e: Collect data on how students travel to school to answer 'What is the most common way to get to school?'
Record the number of siblings each classmate has in a frequency table with tallies and totals
Enter the same data into a spreadsheet with one column for the category and one for the count
topics.p: If {{name}} wants to find out the most popular way kids get to school, can they plan what to ask, collect the answers, and record them neatly in a table?

topics.ds: Carry out a guided statistical investigation for a question of interest: collect categorical or discrete numerical data, represent it in a suitable display and interpret the results in terms of the question
e: With guidance, investigate 'Which playground equipment is used most at lunch?' by tallying observations over three days
Represent the results in a bar graph with a title and labelled axes
Write two sentences answering the investigation question using the data
topics.p: If {{name}}'s class asks 'Which fruit do we eat most at recess?', can they help collect the data, make a graph, and say what the results show?

topics.ds: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set; solve one- and two-step comparison, sum, and difference problems using bar charts, pictograms, and tables
e: Draw a bar graph where each square represents 5 pets
From a scaled pictogram, answer: how many more children chose football than tennis?
Solve a two-step problem: how many votes in total for the top two choices?
topics.p: If {{name}} looked at a bar chart showing how many books different children read last month, could they work out the total, find the difference between the most and least, and draw their own chart with a scale like "each square = 2 books"?

topics.ds: Use digital tools (online survey forms, spreadsheets, data-logging apps) to acquire categorical and discrete numerical data that address a question of interest, and display it as a column graph or other visualisation
e: Create an online survey question to find classmates' favourite sport and collect the responses
Enter survey results in a spreadsheet and make a column graph from them
Interpret the digital graph by describing the most and least popular choices
topics.p: If {{name}} wants to survey their class, can they use a simple online form or spreadsheet to collect the answers and turn them into a graph?

topics.ds: Analyse how effectively different displays or visualisations show and compare data distributions, and describe the shape of a distribution and the variation in the data
e: Compare a column graph and a pictograph of the same data and explain which shows the differences between categories more clearly
Describe a dot plot of hand spans as 'most values cluster around 16 cm with a few much larger'
Explain which display best compares the heights of two classes and why
topics.p: If {{name}} sees the same results shown in two different graphs, can they explain which graph shows the pattern more clearly and describe where most of the results sit?

topics.ds: Conduct a statistical investigation by collecting data through survey responses and other methods, recording and displaying the data with digital tools, and interpreting and communicating the results
e: Design a 3-question survey about screen time and collect responses from at least 15 people
Record the responses in a spreadsheet and create a suitable graph
Present two findings to the class, using the graph as evidence
topics.p: Could {{name}} run their own survey — like asking friends about screen time — put the answers into a spreadsheet graph, and explain what they found?

topics.ds: Solve comparison, sum, and difference problems using information presented in a line graph
e: Read a line graph of temperature over a week and identify the warmest day
Find the difference in rainfall between two months from a line graph
Explain what a rising/falling line means on a time-series graph
topics.p: If {{name}} sees a line graph showing how a plant's height changed over several weeks, can they read off values, spot when it grew fastest, and find the difference between two points?

topics.ds: Complete, read, and interpret information in tables, including timetables
e: Read a bus timetable to find the departure time for a particular stop
Complete a two-way table from given data about favourite sports by gender
Calculate how long a train journey takes using a timetable
topics.p: Can {{name}} read a timetable — like a train or bus timetable — to find out when a journey leaves, arrives, and how long it takes?

topics.ds: Read, write, and use the vocabulary of statistical analysis — mean, median, mode, range, frequency, data, sample, average, chart, table, graph, pie chart, scatter graph, correlation — with understanding of what each term describes
e: Correctly define and calculate the mean, median, mode, and range of a small data set
Use 'outlier' correctly to identify a value that doesn't fit the pattern, and explain its effect on the mean
Use 'correlation' correctly when describing the relationship shown in a scatter graph
topics.p: If {{name}} looked at a set of test scores from their class, could they find the mean, the median, and the range — and explain what each one tells you about how the class did?

topics.ds: Calculate and interpret the mean as an average of a data set
e: Calculate the mean of five test scores: 72, 85, 90, 68, 95
Explain what the mean represents and how it differs from individual data values
Find a missing data value given the mean and all other values
topics.p: If the family scored 6, 8, 7, 5, and 9 on a board game over five rounds, can {{name}} work out the mean (average) score?

topics.ds: Construct and interpret line graphs for continuous data (e.g. temperature over time, plant growth); read intermediate values, identify trends, and solve comparison and difference problems
e: Read values from a line graph showing temperature over a day, including estimating between plotted points
Construct a line graph from a table of continuous data, choosing an appropriate scale and labelling axes correctly
Use a line graph to solve a two-step problem, such as finding the time period with the greatest rate of change
topics.p: If {{name}} recorded the temperature outside every hour for a day, could they plot those readings on a line graph with proper labels — and then use it to answer questions like 'when was it warmest?' or 'how much did it drop between 3pm and 6pm?'

topics.ds: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); use operations on fractions to solve problems involving data in line plots (e.g. redistribute total equally)
e: Create a line plot showing lengths measured to the nearest 1/8 inch
Use the line plot to find the total of all measurements by adding fractions
Solve: 'If the total liquid were redistributed equally among all beakers, how much would each have?'
topics.p: If {{name}} measured the lengths of several objects to the nearest quarter or eighth of an inch and plotted them on a number line, could they use those measurements to work out totals or share amounts equally?

topics.ds: Interpret and construct pie charts: calculate sector angles from data, draw sectors accurately, and read values from pie charts to solve problems
e: Read a pie chart and determine what fraction or percentage of the total each sector represents
Construct a pie chart from given data by calculating sector angles
Use a pie chart to determine the actual quantity represented by each sector given the total
topics.p: Can {{name}} read a pie chart — for example, one showing how a family spends its weekly budget — and use it to answer questions and solve problems?

topics.ds: Plan and conduct a statistical investigation by posing a question or identifying a problem, collecting relevant data, choosing appropriate displays, interpreting the data and communicating findings in context
e: Pose an investigation question such as 'Do Year 5 students sleep less on school nights?' and plan how to collect the data
Choose and justify a display (column graph, dot plot or table) for the collected data
Write a short report that answers the question and states one limitation of the data
topics.p: Could {{name}} come up with their own question — like whether kids sleep less on school nights — plan how to collect the data, and report what they found?

topics.ds: Acquire, validate and represent nominal and ordinal categorical and discrete numerical data using software including spreadsheets, process it (totals, differences), and report on the distribution by its mode and shape in context
e: Check a spreadsheet of survey responses for missing or impossible entries and correct or remove them
Classify 'favourite colour' as nominal and 'rating from 1 to 5' as ordinal and explain the difference
Use spreadsheet formulas to total each category, then report the mode and describe the shape of the column graph
topics.p: If {{name}} collects survey answers in a spreadsheet, can they spot entries that don't make sense, total each category, and describe what the most common answer was?

topics.ds: Calculate the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of a small numerical data set — find the mean, find each value's distance from the mean (a non-negative number: a value equal to the mean has distance 0), then find the mean of those distances; interpret the MAD as the average distance of the values from the mean, stated in the original units of the data (e.g. minutes, cm, points); and use MADs to compare the spread or consistency of two data sets, recognising that a larger MAD means values typically sit further from the mean and that the MAD is 0 only when every value equals the mean
e: Calculate the MAD of 4, 6, 8, 9, 13 (mean 8; distances 4, 2, 0, 1, 5; MAD 2.4), counting the value equal to the mean as a distance of 0
Explain that a MAD of 3 cm for a set of plant heights means the heights are, on average, 3 cm away from the mean height
Decide which of two bowlers, both with a mean score of 120, is more consistent when their MADs are 8 and 21 points, and justify the choice
topics.p: If {{name}} wrote down how many minutes late the school bus was each day for a week, could they work out how far each day was from the average lateness, average those distances, and explain what that number says about how reliable the bus is?

topics.ds: Describe, interpret, and compare observed distributions of a single variable using measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and spread (range), including choosing a suitable average and the effect of outliers; comparisons describe the observed data sets themselves and do not yet scale the difference in centres by a measure of variability or generalise from samples to wider populations
e: Find the mean, median and mode of 3, 5, 5, 6, 11 (6, 5 and 5) and say which average best represents a typical value
Find the range of 12, 14, 15, 15, 48 and explain why the outlier 48 pulls the mean (20.8) well above the median (15)
Compare two classes' spelling scores using their medians and ranges and write one conclusion about which class did better and one about which was more consistent
topics.p: If {{name}} had the test scores of a whole class, could they find the mean, median, and range, and explain what each tells you about how the class performed?

topics.ds: Construct and interpret a box plot on a numerical scale from a five-number summary (minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum), using the stated convention that the whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum values; interpret the median, quartiles, IQR and range, recognising that each whisker and each half of the box represents roughly a quarter of the data however long or short it is drawn; explain what a box plot does not show (individual values, clusters, gaps, the number of values, or the mean); and compare two distributions using their box plots
e: Draw a box plot for the five-number summary 3, 6, 9, 14, 21 on a labelled scale, stating that the whiskers run from the minimum to the maximum, and read the median, quartiles, IQR (8) and range (18) back from a given box plot

Explain that the longer upper whisker (from 14 to 21) shows the top quarter of values is more spread out — not that it contains more values — and reject claims a box plot cannot support, such as 'the mean is 9', 'most values are close to 9' or the exact number of data values

Explain with an example how two data sets can have the same box plot but different shapes (e.g. one with values spread evenly, the other with two clusters separated by a gap), and compare two classes' box plots using their medians and IQRs in context
topics.p: If {{name}} sees box plots comparing how long two classes spent on homework, could they say which class had the higher middle time and which was more spread out — and explain why a longer whisker doesn't mean more children are in that part?

topics.ds: Interpret and compare data sets for nominal and ordinal categorical and discrete and continuous numerical variables using comparative displays (side-by-side column graphs with ordinal categories in a common order, back-to-back dot plots) made with digital tools, processing the data (percentages, ranges) and comparing distributions by mode, range and shape
e: Make a side-by-side column graph in a spreadsheet comparing the favourite sports (nominal) of Year 3 and Year 6 students and state the mode for each group

Compare two classes' ratings of 'How much do you enjoy reading?' (never, sometimes, often, always) as percentages on side-by-side graphs with the categories in the same order, and say which class's ratings sit higher on the scale
Compare two classes' jump distances by mode, range and shape using back-to-back dot plots made with a digital tool
topics.p: If {{name}} has survey results from two classes of different sizes, can they use a spreadsheet to make a side-by-side graph, turn the counts into percentages, and compare the two fairly?

topics.ds: Identify statistically informed arguments in traditional and digital media and critique their methods, data representations (e.g. truncated axes, distorted pictographs, selective data) and conclusions
e: Explain how a bar graph whose vertical axis starts at 90 exaggerates a small difference
Identify the sample size and who was surveyed in a news claim such as '9 out of 10 kids prefer Brand X' and judge whether the conclusion is justified
Rewrite a misleading online headline so that it matches what the data actually show
topics.p: If {{name}} sees an ad saying '9 out of 10 kids prefer this cereal' or a graph with a stretched-out axis, can they ask who was asked and whether the graph makes the difference look bigger than it is?

topics.ds: Describe the distribution of a numerical data set by its centre, spread and overall shape — recognising clusters, gaps, peaks, symmetry or skew (a longer tail on one side) and unusual values — and interpret each feature in the context in which the data were collected, recognising that distributions with similar centres can differ greatly in spread and shape
e: Describe a dot plot of 25 pupils' reaction times by its centre (a typical value), its spread (where most values lie and how far they extend) and its shape — naming any cluster, gap, symmetry or skew and unusual value — and link each feature to the context (e.g. a gap between two groups of times might reflect pupils who had practised and pupils who had not)

Compare two distributions with the same mean — e.g. two classes both averaging 60% on a test, one with scores clustered between 52% and 68%, the other spread from 20% to 95% in two separate clusters — and explain what the shared mean hides and why the difference matters in context

Use the context to judge whether an unusual value is more likely a recording error or a genuine extreme (e.g. a reaction time of 4.2 s among times near 0.3 s), and identify claims the display alone cannot support, such as the reason for a skew or that the same pattern would hold for a different group
topics.p: If {{name}} sees a dot plot of how long children in their class took to run 100 m, could they describe where most times bunch up, how spread out they are and whether there are any odd ones out — and suggest a sensible reason for what they see?

topics.ds: Construct and interpret dot plots for numerical data sets of any kind (counts, scores, times or measurements), extending earlier measurement line plots: draw a number-line scale with equal intervals that runs from at least the minimum to the maximum value, including values nobody recorded so that gaps stay visible; place one dot per observation, stacking repeated values in evenly spaced columns; label the scale with the attribute and its units; and read the plot to find how often a value occurs, the minimum, maximum and most common values, and the total number of observations, recognising that the height of a stack is a count of observations, not a data value
e: Draw a dot plot of 20 pupils' numbers of books read last month (values 0 to 12) on a scale marked 0, 1, 2, …, 12, leaving the empty value 7 visible as a gap and stacking the four 3s evenly
Read from a dot plot that the value 5 occurs 6 times, the minimum is 0, the maximum is 12 and the most common value is 5
Explain that a stack of 6 dots above 5 means six pupils each read 5 books, not that someone read 6 books, and count all the dots to give the number of pupils
topics.p: If {{name}} asked 20 classmates how many books they read last month, could they draw a dot plot with one dot per person stacked above the right number on a number line — and then say how many classmates read exactly 5 books?

topics.ds: Construct and interpret histograms for continuous or numerical data grouped into equal-width class intervals on a continuous number-line scale, with no gaps between bars; state the interval-boundary convention used (e.g. 140 ≤ h < 150, so a value of exactly 150 belongs to the next interval); read frequencies from bar heights; describe the distribution shown; and explain how a histogram differs from a bar chart of categories. Unequal-width intervals and frequency density are not included.
e: Group 30 pupils' heights into equal-width 10 cm intervals (130 ≤ h < 140, 140 ≤ h < 150, …), stating that a height of exactly 150 cm is counted in the 150 ≤ h < 160 interval, and draw the histogram with a continuous horizontal scale, touching bars and labelled axes

Read frequencies accurately from a histogram (e.g. how many pupils are at least 150 cm but less than 160 cm, and how many are shorter than 150 cm in total) and describe the distribution's centre, spread and shape in context

Explain why a histogram's bars touch and sit on a numerical scale while a bar chart of categories (e.g. favourite sport) has gaps and an order that could be rearranged — and identify claims the histogram cannot support, such as the exact height of the tallest pupil or how many pupils are exactly 145 cm tall
topics.p: If {{name}} sorted the heights of everyone in their class into groups like '130 cm up to 140 cm' and '140 cm up to 150 cm', could they draw a histogram with the bars touching — and explain why it isn't the same kind of chart as a bar chart of favourite colours?

topics.ds: Construct and interpret frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, and vertical line charts for both categorical and grouped numerical data, choosing appropriate representations for the data type
e: Construct a grouped frequency table from raw continuous data, choosing appropriate class intervals
Draw a pie chart by calculating the angle for each category
Interpret a bar chart comparing two data sets and draw a conclusion about the difference
topics.p: When {{name}} collects data for a project, can they choose the right type of chart to display it — and draw it accurately with correct labels and a suitable scale?

topics.ds: Distinguish a population from a sample drawn from it; explain why a convenient or biased sample (choosing whoever is easiest to reach, volunteers, or a group linked to the answer) can misrepresent the population; explain that random selection gives every member of the population an equal chance of being chosen, which tends to produce representative samples — while recognising that any single random sample can still, by chance, be unrepresentative
e: In a described survey (e.g. a school asks 40 of its 800 pupils about the lunch menu), identify the population and the sample, and explain why a sample is used instead of asking everyone

Identify the selection bias in a sampling method (e.g. asking people leaving a gym how often they exercise, or surveying only the lunch queue on pizza day), explain the direction in which it would likely distort the result, and propose a better method using random selection from the whole population (e.g. drawing names from the full school register)
